decisive_items: invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
well-defined hypodense lesion measuring 4.6 × 3.4 cm with fat density in the sigmoid-colon wall protruding into the lumen
response.rationale: The CT finding of colonic invagination with a fat-density lead point is pathognomonic for intussusception, likely due to a lipoma. Other candidates lack this specific imaging correlate.

rejected.why: No evidence of chronic inflammation or IBD-specific findings; fat-density mass and intussusception are not typical.
Fat density on CT is not characteristic of adenocarcinoma; normal CEA and lack of constitutional symptoms further argue against cancer.
No diverticula or inflammatory changes on imaging; symptoms are better explained by intussusception.
Too nonspecific; the imaging clearly demonstrates intussusception, which is the most precise diagnosis.
